context: Request: the firm's first traditional, non-SPAC IPO, with offering documents and proof the deal closed. Rubric: 1037-00001 (Solstice Biomedical ADS IPO, closed March 2023), an offering document, a closing deliverable, and a precision criterion that fails when another matter (here 1010-00002, Arbor Health, closed Feb 2024) is called qualifying.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Whole-store glob.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Attempt 2: script prints every matter's file list (about 545K characters). The end review's label note names folder listing, and the next stage is declared that way.

stages.stage: Search file names for request keywords
stages.note: declared: List matter folders. Counts and lists matter folders, then a path regex for offering, registration, underwriting and closing words grouped per matter. The review flags the file-name-only screen; its label note names the text scan, which the next stage declares.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Store-wide extraction script writes 761 hit lines to a file; the printed part is cut at about 40K characters, which the review flags.

stages.stage: Search file names for request keywords
stages.note: declared: Scan document text with an extraction script (attempt 2). A per-matter path regex for strong offering words over the saved list, not a text scan, as the review notes.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: Reads prospectus, underwriting, cross-receipt and closing papers of six candidates in two parallel batches, including the later closed offering and the earlier closed depositary-share offering. The review flags many unopened matters and that the later offering is only a comparison point.

stages.stage: Write the response
stages.note: Writes the earliest closed offering with its executed offering documents and closing certificate and checklist; the later closed offering appears in the chronology as a later qualifying deal.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Re-reads the response and checks cited paths exist.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Attempt 2: re-opens five cited and excluded sources and edits one paragraph on how first is defined.

stages.stage: Finish the run
stages.note: Calls finish.

runs.sequence: List files in the document store → Search file names for request keywords → Scan document text with an extraction script → Search file names for request keywords → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → Write the response → Check or revise the response → Finish the run
runs.failure_point: Read the later closed offering as a comparison and wrote it into the chronology as a second qualifying traditional offering.

first_error.critic_note: The write review asked only to check facts and to state each exclusion reason (naming the later offering's exclusion reason); no review named the later offering being presented as qualifying.
first_error.why: The answer names the earliest closed offering correctly but also describes a later closed operating-company offering, read at [34]-[43], as a qualifying traditional offering in its chronology, so the answer asserts a second qualifying matter.

runs.failure_point: Wrote the later closed offering as a later qualifying traditional offering.

first_error.critic_note: The write review asked to confirm the date ordering against every other candidate and to state exclusion reasons; the last review endorsed the answer. None named the later offering being called qualifying.
first_error.why: The answer names the earliest closed offering correctly but also describes a later closed operating-company offering, read at [30]-[42], as a qualifying traditional offering in its chronology, so the answer asserts a second qualifying matter.

divergence: All three runs fail the same way at the write stage. Each found and read the earliest closed operating-company offering (executed underwriting, deposit and registration-rights agreements plus closing certificates and checklist) and the later closed offering, and wrote the earliest as first; each also described the later one as a qualifying traditional offering in its chronology, which the precision check counts as a second qualifying matter. The reviews never named this: they pushed for wider coverage and for exclusion reasons for every competitor, which kept the later offering in the answer as a compared, qualifying deal. No label note or agent-defined stage played a role.
